citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
Daily observations were not conducted on a female coati nursing offspring after she was given some pitted fruit on Aug
23, 2026. She was not observed on the 24th and found dead behind an exhibit rock on Aug 25, 2026 in the evening with a
bloated body and damage done to the nipple area where it was assumed the offspring tried to nurse. Lack of daily
observations failed to observe the mom had died or that the offspring were not nursing adequately.
The facility must have an ability to perform daily observations on all animals to assess their health and well being and
have a mechanism of direct and frequent communication with the attending veterinarian so that timely and accurate
information on problems of animal health, behavior, and well-being is conveyed to the attending veterinarian.
Correct by: Sept 24, 2026

Areas of chain link around the goat enclosure are in disrepair. Sections of chain link for one gate and along the back side
of the goat enclosure are bent and broken with wires protruding into the enclosure which could potentially cause injury to
the goats.
The indoor and outdoor housing facilities shall be maintained in good repair to protect the animals from injury and to
contain the animals.

Feces are not being removed from the goat and coati mundi enclosure as often as necessary to keep the area clean and
prevent contamination of the animals as they move throughout their enclosure.
***The shelter area for the goats has an accumulation of feces throughout the area and outside the shelter that needs to
be cleaned. The mineral block is on a dirty pan with feces and there is no clean area in the shelter where the goats can
lay down without laying in their feces.
*** The four juvenile coatis are in a room where the floor, their crate, blankets and shelf are covered in feces caked into
the wood and floor. There is a strong odor in the room and the animals are limited in where they can move to avoid
contact with fecal material.
Feces shall be removed from primary enclosures as often as necessary to prevent contamination of the animals
contained therein and to minimize disease hazards and to reduce odors. These enclosures need to be addressed for the
health of the animals.
Correct by: Sept 2, 2026

The facility does not have an effective program for the control of rodents in the barn area housing the pigs, rabbit, wallaby,
porcupine and cavy. Despite the multiple live traps around the area, there is evidence of rodents destroying and living in
the walls and feces throughout the area. This barn and other animal areas need to be addressed to prevent excessive
rodents living and breeding in the area which can carry disease hazards.
A safe and effective program for the control of insects, ectoparasites, and avian and mammalian pests shall be
established and maintained for the health of the animals.
Correct by: Oct 1, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
